html:
SMTO-BOOT-0048 — SMTO can't save data because its disk is read-only

GUID: 12b274b8-2be9-40ba-9010-94ee0192e48d
Slug: startup-storage-read-only
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: startup

What happened

  • SMTO can see the disk where it keeps its data, but the disk is set so nothing can be written to it. SMTO needs to write there to start.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If SMTO keeps its data on an external or network drive, make sure the drive is connected and its write-protect switch, if it has one, is off. A disconnected or write-protected drive can look read-only to SMTO.
  2. Ask the person who manages this computer to make the disk writable again. A disk can switch itself to read-only after it finds errors. Restarting SMTO alone doesn't change a disk that won't accept changes.
  3. When the disk is writable, select Start again on this screen if you see it, or start SMTO the way you normally do. Starting again only repeats the startup; it doesn't repeat any of your earlier work.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and your conversations appear.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't move or delete SMTO's data folder; if the disk turned read-only because of errors, have it checked before anything else is changed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Startup failed because the operating system rejected a write with EROFS: the volume holding the Server's state is mounted read-only.

What this means

  • Runtime restoration and ownership require writable storage. A read-only mount or filesystem state prevents these operations even if file permissions appear correct.

Why this can happen

  • Runtime restoration and ownership require writable storage. A read-only mount or filesystem state prevents these operations even if file permissions appear correct.

How to diagnose it

  • The operating system rejected a startup write to read-only storage.
  • The runtime directory is writable and the controller acquires ownership.

How to fix it

  • Find the mount holding AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR (findmnt -T on that directory) and why it is read-only: a ro mount option, a filesystem remounted read-only after I/O errors (check dmesg and run fsck offline), a write-protected device, or a read-only container volume. Restore a writable mount without moving or deleting the state directory, then restart.
  • Ask the host administrator to restore a writable runtime volume or correct its mount configuration. Preserve the state directory and restart after storage is healthy.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition and run the diagnostic again. Rechecking does not replay tasks or completed operations.

How to verify the fix

  • The runtime directory is writable and the controller acquires ownership.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
